subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: Chinua Achebe and African Short Fiction
description: A 60-second lesson on Chinua Achebe and African Short Fiction.

hook.text: Chinua Achebe used the short story to show that African literature could speak for itself, without Western filters.

buildup.text: His stories explored post-colonial Nigeria: corruption, cultural clash, and the aftermath of independence.

discovery.text: In Civil Peace, a man who survived the Biafran War is robbed of his compensation money by armed thieves.

twist.text: Achebe rejected the label 'Third World writer,' insisting that African stories were universal, not exotic curiosities.

climax.text: He showed that short fiction could dismantle colonial narratives and build new literary traditions from within.

punchline.text: He refused to let outsiders define African stories.

quiz.question: What did Achebe insist about African literature?
options: African stories were universal, not exotic curiosities
It should only be written in African languages
